clinical.citation: Pathogenic variants in MAEA disrupt DNA replication fork stability and are associated with developmental abnormalities in humans (PMID: 40880485)
clinical.diagnostic_reason: Disease-linked variants shown to be defective in replication stress response; associated with developmental disorder involving microcephaly, craniofacial abnormalities, ocular defects, and heart malformations

clinical.citation: Loss of CTLH component MAEA impairs DNA repair and replication and leads to developmental delay (PMID: 41420108)
clinical.diagnostic_reason: Eight patients identified with variants in MAEA presenting with neurodevelopmental disorder (DIADEM - Developmental delay and Intellectual disability Associated with DEfects in MAEA); patient-derived cell lines show defects in HR-dependent DNA repair and replication fork restart

model_organism.citation: Loss of CTLH component MAEA impairs DNA repair and replication and leads to developmental delay (PMID: 41420108)
phenotypes: defective replication fork restart and protection
reduced RAD51 loading at DNA damage sites

model_organism.citation: MAEA is an E3 ubiquitin ligase promoting autophagy and maintenance of haematopoietic stem cells (PMID: 33947846)
phenotypes: stabilized surface expression of haematopoietic cytokine receptors (MPL, FLT3)

model_organism.citation: Maea expressed by macrophages, but not erythroblasts, maintains postnatal murine bone marrow erythroblastic islands (PMID: 30674470)
phenotypes: severe reduction of bone marrow macrophages (macrophage-specific knockout)
impaired in vivo erythroblastic island formation (macrophage-specific knockout)

model_organism.citation: maea affects head formation through ß-catenin degradation during early Xenopus laevis development (PMID: 36444483)
phenotypes: reduced expression of Wnt target genes (nodal3.1, sia1)

biological.citation: E3 ligase MAEA-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of PHD3 promotes glioblastoma progression (PMID: 36882523)
biological.summary: MAEA functions as an E3 ubiquitin ligase that targets PHD3 at K159 for K48-linked polyubiquitination and degradation, leading to HIF-1α stabilization and enhanced stemness and temozolomide resistance in glioblastoma cells. High MAEA expression correlates with glioma recurrence and poor prognosis.
biological.sample_size: clinical primary and recurrent glioma samples
biological.significance: associated with recurrence and poor prognosis

biological.citation: Pathogenic variants in MAEA disrupt DNA replication fork stability and are associated with developmental abnormalities in humans (PMID: 40880485)
biological.summary: MAEA is a core component of the CTLH E3 ubiquitin ligase complex that regulates homologous recombination by mediating ubiquitylation of Ku80, enabling its removal from replication fork ends and facilitating RAD51 loading. Loss of MAEA impairs RAD51 recruitment and causes increased sensitivity to replication stress and excessive nascent DNA degradation.
biological.significance: disease-linked variants (R34C, E349G, Y394D, M396R) show defective replication stress response

biological.citation: The E3 ubiquitin ligase MAEA promotes macrophage phagocytosis and inhibits gastrointestinal cancer progression by mediating PARP1 ubiquitination and degradation (PMID: 39990651)
biological.summary: MAEA mediates K48-linked ubiquitination and degradation of PARP1 in gastrointestinal cancer cells, impairing proliferation and chemoresistance. MAEA also suppresses M2 macrophage polarization and enhances macrophage phagocytic activity. Reduced MAEA expression in GIC patients correlates with worse disease-free and overall survival.
biological.significance: reduced MAEA associated with worse survival outcomes

biological.citation: The CTLH ubiquitin ligase substrates ZMYND19 and MKLN1 negatively regulate mTORC1 at the lysosomal membrane (PMID: 41315365)
biological.summary: MAEA is the catalytic subunit of the CTLH E3 ligase complex that negatively regulates mTORC1 signaling by ubiquitinating and degrading ZMYND19 and MKLN1, which inhibit mTORC1 activity at the lysosomal membrane. MAEA knockout in EBV-associated gastric carcinoma cells synergistically blocks proliferation when combined with PI3K inhibition.
biological.significance: MAEA among top CRISPR screen hits for PI3K/mTOR pathway dysregulation

biological.citation: MAEA is an E3 ubiquitin ligase promoting autophagy and maintenance of haematopoietic stem cells (PMID: 33947846)
biological.summary: MAEA is a membrane-associated E3 ubiquitin ligase essential for hematopoietic stem cell maintenance and quiescence. MAEA deletion impairs HSC quiescence and causes lethal myeloproliferative syndrome by stabilizing cytokine receptors (MPL, FLT3) and impairing autophagy flux. MAEA restricts cytokine receptor signaling via autophagy-mediated degradation.
biological.significance: Maea deletion leads to lethal myeloproliferative syndrome

biological.citation: maea affects head formation through β-catenin degradation during early Xenopus laevis development (PMID: 36444483)
biological.summary: Xenopus laevis MAEA (maea) is an E3 ubiquitin ligase that promotes β-catenin ubiquitination and degradation, regulating canonical Wnt signaling during early embryogenesis. maea.S overexpression enlarges head structures while knockdown interferes with head formation, demonstrating a role in axis and head formation.
biological.significance: maea.S overexpression enlarges head structures; knockdown impairs head formation

biological.citation: TBC1D14 inhibits autophagy to suppress lymph node metastasis in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma by downregulating macrophage erythroblast attacher (PMID: 35342354)
biological.summary: MAEA expression negatively correlates with TBC1D14 expression in HNSCC. MAEA overexpression reverses TBC1D14-induced autophagy suppression and promotes migration and invasion. MAEA is downregulated in HNSCC with lymph node metastasis, and TBC1D14 suppresses autophagy and metastasis by downregulating MAEA.
biological.sample_size: HNSCC tissue samples and cell lines
biological.significance: MAEA expression inversely correlates with TBC1D14; lower MAEA associated with lymph node metastasis

biological.citation: RANBP9 and RANBP10 cooperate in regulating non-small cell lung cancer proliferation (PMID: 40883813)
biological.summary: MAEA is the catalytic subunit of the CTLH E3 ligase complex; RANBP9 and RANBP10 (Scorpins) are essential CTLH components that regulate NSCLC proliferation. The RANBP9/RANBP10 ratio modulates CTLH complex ubiquitylation output, with higher RANBP9/RANBP10 ratio associated with greater proliferation.
biological.sample_size: NSCLC cell lines and patient tumors
biological.significance: higher RANBP9/RANBP10 ratio associated with greater proliferation in NSCLC

biological.citation: ASHG 2017 - Whole exome sequencing and exome array genotyping in 3,943 Korean type 2 diabetes cases and controls
biological.summary: MAEA was validated as a known common variant locus associated with type 2 diabetes in Korean populations through exome sequencing and genotyping array analysis. MAEA variants showed genome-wide significant association with T2D risk.

biological.citation: ASHG 2011 - Comprehensive evaluation of type 2 diabetes susceptibility in the Japanese population by genome-wide imputation analysis using the 1000 Genomes Project data
biological.summary: SNPs in the MAEA region (rs730831, rs4974585, rs4974586) were identified as possibly associated with type 2 diabetes in Japanese populations through genome-wide imputation analysis. Combined P values reached genome-wide significance with OR ranging from 1.18 to 1.25.
